newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Services push up Philippine June inflation.
newsitem.headline: Services push up Philippine June inflation.

text.p: Philippine inflation in June was fuelled by a rise in commodity prices as well as services, the National Statistics Office said on Friday.
Last month's increase was 4.8 percent against 4.2 percent in May.
The figure was higher than the market and the Central Bank had expected. A Reuters poll of Manila brokerages on Thursday had shown the market expected June inflation to be 4.26 percent.
On Monday, the Philippine Central Bank said June inflation was expected to be 3.9 percent.
The National Statistics Office gave the following details for the various ingredients of the inflation basket:
* All the commodity groups registered year-on-year increases in inflation rates in June.

* The services index rose by 13.7 percent from 11.7 percent year-on-year. This could be attributed to the increases in tuition fees and prices of school supplies timed with the opening of classes in June along with higher charges in medical and dental services and personal services.

* The housing and repairs index rose by nine percent from 8.8 percent in May; food and beverages 1.7 percent from 1.2 percent; fuel, light and water 8.3 percent from 7.9 percent; clothing 3.6 percent from 3.4 percent; and miscellaneous items 1.8 percent from 1.5 percent.
* The inflation rate for food alone rose to 1.4 percent from one percent in May.

* Month-on-month inflation rates were higher for all the commodity groups: Food, beverages and tobacco 0.6 percent after it decreased by 0.2 percent last month; services 6.1 percent from 0.4 percent; housing and repairs 0.8 percent from 0.2 percent; fuel, light and water 0.4 percent from minus 0.6 percent; miscellaneous items 0.2 percent from 0.1 percent; and clothing 0.4 percent from 0.1 percent.
* The services index registered the highest month-on-month rate at 6.1 percent in the Philippines, 12.2 percent in Manila and 3.5 percent in areas outside Metro Manila.
